title: Why More International Students Are Choosing India in 2026?
excerpt: Students from 175+ countries are choosing India for their degree — and the numbers are growing at 8% per year. Here are the 8 real reasons why, with honest cost comparisons.

The Study Destination That Most Students Never Seriously Consider — But Should

When international students and their families think about studying abroad, the conversation almost always starts with the same four names: Australia, the UK, the USA, Canada. India rarely comes up. And yet, students from over 175 countries are currently enrolled in Indian universities — a figure that has grown by 42% in recent years and is projected to increase by 8% annually through 2030, according to QS Quacquarelli Symonds.

Something is clearly changing. The international students choosing India in 2026 are not doing so by accident or by default. They are making a deliberate, strategic decision — often after carefully comparing costs, course quality, career outcomes, and long-term options. And when you look at the numbers honestly, their reasoning is difficult to argue with.

📊
India is now the world's second-largest higher education system With over 50 million students enrolled in higher education and more than 1,000 universities, India operates one of the largest and most diverse academic ecosystems on the planet. The size of the system means there is a course, a campus, and a career pathway for virtually every academic background and budget.

This guide is not a promotional piece for India. It is an honest look at the eight real reasons why more international students are choosing India for their degree in 2026 — and who this choice is genuinely right for.

8 Real Reasons International Students Are Choosing India in 2026

Reason 01
The Cost Difference Is Extraordinary

This is, for most students, the most compelling factor — and the numbers speak for themselves. A four-year B.Tech degree from an IIT costs between INR 8 and 10 lakh in total tuition fees. A one-year Master's in the UK costs between GBP 18,000 and 35,000 in tuition alone — before accommodation, food, or transport. The same program in Australia runs to AUD 28,000–45,000 per year. India is not marginally cheaper. For many programs, India is 5 to 10 times cheaper than Western destinations for equivalent academic quality.

🇮🇳 India — Full Degree Cost
B.Tech (IIT, 4 years): INR 8–10 Lakh
MBBS (5.5 years): INR 40–65 Lakh
MBA (IIM, 2 years): INR 20–35 Lakh
Living costs/month: INR 12,000–28,000
🌍 Equivalent Cost Abroad
B.Eng (UK, 3 years): GBP 54,000–90,000
MBBS (Australia): AUD 280,000–350,000
MBA (UK, 1 year): GBP 30,000–60,000
Living costs/month: GBP 1,200–2,000+

For families in South Asia, Africa, and Southeast Asia who aspire to an internationally recognized degree but cannot comfortably fund full Western tuition and living costs, India represents the most realistic pathway to a high-quality education without taking on unmanageable debt.

Reason 02
IITs, IIMs, and AIIMS Carry Genuine Global Prestige

India's premier institutions are not second-tier alternatives to Western universities. The Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs) consistently appear in global top-200 engineering rankings. IIT Bombay and IIT Delhi are regularly ranked among the top 100 universities in Asia. The Indian Institutes of Management (IIMs) at Ahmedabad, Bangalore, and Calcutta are recognized among Asia's best business schools. A degree from IIT or IIM carries weight in job markets across the USA, UK, Singapore, the UAE, and Australia — often as much as a degree from a mid-ranked Western university.

For international students in engineering, technology, business, or medicine, India's top institutions offer a globally competitive academic experience at a fraction of the cost of their Western equivalents. Crucially, IIT graduates routinely receive placement offers from multinational companies — with average packages at IIT Bombay reaching INR 23.50 lakh per annum, and some graduates securing offers above INR 1 crore per annum.

Reason 03
MBBS in India Is One of the Most Sought-After Medical Degrees Globally

Medical education in India is a major draw for international students — particularly from neighboring countries and Africa. Indian MBBS programs are recognized by the World Health Organization (WHO), the National Medical Commission (NMC) of India, ECFMG (USA), and the General Medical Council (GMC) of the UK. This means that a medical degree from a recognized Indian institution can open doors to licensing examinations and medical careers in multiple countries worldwide.

The 5.5-year MBBS program in India — including a mandatory one-year internship — costs between INR 40 and 65 lakh in total at private institutions, with government medical colleges significantly cheaper. Compare this to MBBS or equivalent medical degrees in Australia (AUD 280,000–350,000+) or the UK, and the cost differential is stark. For students aiming for a medical career who cannot access or afford Western medical school fees, India is increasingly the most logical choice.

🏥
Indian medical degrees are recognized for licensing in multiple countries Graduates of NMC-recognized Indian medical colleges can appear for the FMGE/NExT exam to practice in India, the USMLE for the USA, and PLAB for the UK. This global portability of an Indian MBBS degree makes it one of the most strategically versatile medical qualifications available at this price point anywhere in the world.
Reason 04
Fully Funded Scholarships Are Available — and Not Widely Known

The Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR), operating under India's Ministry of External Affairs, offers one of the most comprehensive and underutilized scholarship programs for international students in the world. The ICCR General Scholarship Scheme provides fully funded places — covering tuition, accommodation, and a monthly living allowance — to students from Asian, African, and Latin American countries at undergraduate, postgraduate, and doctoral level.

Beyond the ICCR, the Government of India's Study in India (SII) Scholarship Program offers tuition fee waivers of 25%, 50%, 75%, and 100% at NAAC-accredited partner institutions for international students in undergraduate, postgraduate, diploma, and certificate programs. Applications for the 2026–27 academic year were open from February through April 2026, with students joining between June and August.

  • ICCR General Scholarship Scheme: Fully funded — tuition, accommodation, living allowance, and travel support. Open to students from selected Asian, African, and Latin American countries for UG, PG, and PhD programs.
  • Study in India (SII) Scholarship: Tuition fee waivers of 25–100% at NAAC-ranked partner institutions. Available for UG, PG, diploma, and certificate programs across all subjects.
  • IGIDR Scholarship: Funded by the Reserve Bank of India for students from selected Asian countries pursuing graduate and postgraduate programs at the Indira Gandhi Institute of Development Research.
  • University-specific scholarships: Most major Indian universities offer merit-based scholarships and fee waivers to outstanding international applicants. These are often available in addition to government scholarship schemes.
Reason 05
English Is the Primary Medium of Instruction

One of the most common misconceptions about studying in India is that language will be a barrier. In reality, the overwhelming majority of undergraduate and postgraduate programs at Indian universities — particularly in engineering, medicine, business, and technology — are taught entirely in English. India has one of the largest English-speaking populations in the world, and its higher education system has been built on English-medium instruction for decades.

This is significant for international students from South Asia, Africa, and Southeast Asia who are already comfortable in English but may find the French, German, or other European-medium programs at competing affordable destinations more challenging to access. No IELTS or TOEFL score is required for most Indian university admissions — a practical advantage for students who are fluent in English but have not yet sat a formal proficiency examination.

Reason 06
India's Economy and Tech Sector Create Real Career Opportunities

India is no longer just a study destination — it is increasingly a career destination. India's economy is one of the fastest-growing in the world, with its IT, fintech, healthcare, and manufacturing sectors expanding at a pace that is generating substantial demand for skilled graduates. Bengaluru, Hyderabad, and Pune have emerged as major global technology hubs, with multinational companies including Google, Microsoft, Amazon, Deloitte, and Goldman Sachs all maintaining significant Indian operations.

For international students who complete their degree in India and wish to build an initial career in a high-growth economy before moving on to a Western destination, India's graduate job market offers a compelling entry point. Starting salaries at top Indian firms for IIT or IIM graduates are increasingly competitive, and the experience of working in one of the world's largest economies is genuinely valued by employers globally.

💡
The India-first career strategy Some international students deliberately complete their undergraduate degree in India, spend 2–3 years in the Indian job market to build their CV and savings, and then apply for postgraduate programs in Australia, the UK, or New Zealand. They arrive at the postgraduate level with work experience, savings, and a stronger academic profile — making them more competitive for both university admission and post-study employment.
Reason 07
The Admission Process Is Straightforward — No IELTS Required

Western university applications have become increasingly complex in 2026. The UK demands significantly higher financial proof. Australia has introduced the Genuine Student requirement with stricter documentation. The USA's visa interview appointments are extremely limited and wait times are long. By contrast, the admission process at Indian universities is notably more straightforward for international students.

Most Indian universities do not require IELTS or TOEFL scores from international students applying for English-medium programs, since instruction and assessment have historically been conducted in English. No No Objection Certificate (NOC) process comparable to what some governments require for Western study is needed from most source countries. Student visas for India are processed relatively quickly, and the overall application-to-arrival timeline is typically shorter than for Western destinations.

Reason 08
India Is a Strategic Stepping Stone — Not Just a Final Destination

Perhaps the most compelling reason of all for strategic students: studying in India does not close any doors — it opens them. An undergraduate degree from a recognized Indian institution is accepted for postgraduate admission at universities in the UK, Australia, New Zealand, and the USA. Indian engineering, nursing, and accounting graduates regularly have their credentials recognized by professional bodies in Australia and New Zealand for the purposes of skills assessment and PR applications.

For students whose long-term goal is permanent residency in Australia or New Zealand, the India-first strategy can be financially transformative. By completing an undergraduate degree in India at a fraction of the cost, students can preserve their family's financial resources for the more strategically important postgraduate year abroad — during which they are older, more experienced, and more competitive for both graduate employment and PR applications.

🎯
The India-then-Abroad Pathway — Admizz Education's Strategic Recommendation Complete your undergraduate degree in India (nursing, engineering, IT, or accounting). Work for 1–2 years to build savings and experience. Apply for a postgraduate program in Australia or New Zealand. Arrive with a stronger profile, lower debt, and a clear head start on your PR journey. This pathway consistently delivers better long-term outcomes for cost-conscious families than starting directly at the postgraduate level abroad with no experience and maximum debt.

Top Indian Institutions International Students Should Know

India's higher education landscape spans thousands of institutions — from government-funded universities of international standing to private colleges of varying quality. For international students, focusing on NAAC-accredited and NIRF-ranked institutions is essential for ensuring that your qualification is recognized abroad. Here are the key institution categories and their best-known names.

Engineering
IITs (23 campuses)
Indian Institutes of Technology. IIT Bombay, Delhi, Madras, Kanpur, and Kharagpur are globally ranked. Total B.Tech fees: INR 8–10 lakh (4 years).
Business
IIMs (21 campuses)
Indian Institutes of Management. IIM Ahmedabad, Bangalore, and Calcutta rank among Asia's best MBA schools. 2-year MBA fees: INR 20–35 lakh.
Medicine
AIIMS & Medical Colleges
All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) is WHO and NMC recognized. Private NMC-approved colleges charge INR 40–65 lakh for the full 5.5-year MBBS.
Science & Research
IISc Bangalore
Indian Institute of Science — consistently ranked India's top research university and among the world's best for science and engineering research.
Multidisciplinary
University of Delhi, JNU, BHU
Central universities with strong arts, social sciences, law, and humanities programs. Government-funded with low tuition and active international student communities.
Private Universities
BITS Pilani, Ashoka, Shiv Nadar
Well-regarded private universities offering international-standard facilities, English-medium instruction, and active industry placement partnerships.

Is India the Right Choice for You? An Honest Assessment

India is a genuinely excellent choice for some international students. It is not the right choice for all of them. Here is an honest breakdown of who India tends to work best for — and where it may not be the most suitable option.

Your Situation Is India a Good Fit? Why
Budget-conscious family, strong academic record ✅ Excellent fit Top-quality education at a fraction of Western costs. IIT / IIM credentials are globally respected.
Aspiring medical student (MBBS) ✅ Excellent fit NMC/WHO-recognized degrees. Affordable vs Western medical education. Globally portable with licensing exams.
Long-term goal is PR in Australia or New Zealand ✅ Strong strategic fit India-first strategy reduces total debt. Indian UG credentials are recognized for postgrad admission and skills assessment abroad.
Seeking post-study work rights immediately after graduation ⚠️ Limited India does not offer a formal post-study work visa route comparable to Australia, UK, or New Zealand. Working rights are limited on a student visa.
Goal is to live and work in India long-term ✅ Good fit India's growing economy, particularly in IT, finance, and healthcare, offers strong career opportunities for international graduates who wish to stay.
Primarily motivated by post-study PR pathway ⚠️ Not ideal as a sole strategy Use India as a foundation, then move to Australia or NZ for postgraduate study and PR. India alone does not provide a direct PR pathway to Western countries.

Frequently Asked Questions

Are degrees from Indian universities accepted for postgraduate admission in Australia, UK, and New Zealand?
Yes — undergraduate degrees from recognized and NAAC-accredited Indian universities are accepted for postgraduate admission at universities in Australia, the UK, and New Zealand, provided the student meets the academic requirements of the target program. IIT and IIM graduates are particularly well regarded internationally. For professional qualifications such as engineering and nursing, Indian credentials can also be assessed by Australian and New Zealand professional bodies for the purposes of skilled migration applications.
Do I need an IELTS score to study in India as an international student?
Most Indian universities do not require IELTS or TOEFL scores from international students applying for English-medium programs, as English is the primary medium of instruction in Indian higher education. Some institutions may request proof of English proficiency from students whose previous education was conducted in a different language, but this is assessed on a case-by-case basis. This is a meaningful practical advantage for students who are fluent in English but have not yet completed a formal proficiency exam.
What is the ICCR scholarship and how do I apply?
The ICCR (Indian Council for Cultural Relations) scholarship is a fully funded scholarship program offered by the Government of India to students from selected Asian, African, and Latin American countries. It covers tuition fees, accommodation, and a monthly living allowance for undergraduate, postgraduate, and doctoral programs at Indian universities. Applications are submitted through the ICCR A2A online portal, which typically opens between February and April each year for the following academic session. Admizz Education can help you identify whether your country of origin is eligible and guide you through the application process.
Can an MBBS degree from India be used to practice medicine in other countries?
Yes — but with licensing requirements specific to each country. An MBBS from an NMC-recognized Indian medical college is accepted for the FMGE/NExT licensing examination required to practice medicine in India, the USMLE (United States Medical Licensing Examination) for the USA, and the PLAB examination for the UK. Many Indian medical colleges are also listed in the World Directory of Medical Schools (WDOMS), which is the reference used by licensing authorities globally. Graduates should verify the specific licensing pathway for their target country before selecting an institution.
